situation.problem_text:
Topic: The Geometric Intuition of the Cross Product

Target audience: University students (Engineering/Mathematics/Physics)

Section: section_1 — Prerequisites: Vectors in 3D Space

Lecture lines:
Consider two vectors, u and v, in 3D.
They define a parallelogram in space.
This shape is our geometric foundation.

Planned animations:
Display 3D coordinate system in #FFFFFF color.
Label the x, y, z axes clearly.
Represent a vector v as an arrow from origin.

Section: section_2 — Definition of the Cross Product

Lecture lines:
The cross product creates a new vector.
This vector is perpendicular to the plane.
Its magnitude equals the parallelogram's area.

Planned animations:
Show two vectors a and b in space.
Draw a resultant vector c perpendicular to a and b.
Label c as the cross product a x b.

Section: section_3 — Geometric Intuition & Determinants

Lecture lines:
The cross product is a determinant.
Zero area means vectors are collinear.
It measures how independent vectors are.

Planned animations:
Display a 2D parallelogram formed by vectors a and b.
Highlight the area represented by the cross product magnitude.
Show the determinant formula for the cross product area.
Illustrate the right-hand rule for the resulting vector direction.
Animate the change in area as vectors a and b rotate.

Section: section_4 — Linear Transformations and Orientation

Lecture lines:
Cross products define linear transformations.
They map vectors to a new space.
This preserves coordinate system handedness.

Planned animations:
Show a grid transformation matrix applying to basis vectors.
Illustrate the change in volume/orientation from transformation.
Highlight the cross product as a linear transformation property.

Section: section_5 — Summary & Application

Lecture lines:
Cross product equals perpendicular vector area.
It is crucial for calculating torque.
Force times lever arm yields rotation.

Planned animations:
Summarize key points: vector definition, formula, and geometry.
Highlight the cross product in physics/engineering applications.
Review the orientation-dependent nature of the cross product.

Use argument unpacking (e.g., *self.mobjects) when passing the scene's internal list to animation constructors like FadeOut to avoid TypeErrors.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
